sub_unit_name: Gaseous fuels - composition and uses of natural gas, LPG and CNG

content.title: Gaseous Fuels
content.description: Gaseous fuels are fuels that exist in the gaseous state under normal conditions and produce heat energy upon combustion. They burn cleanly, have high calorific value, and are easy to transport through pipelines.

content.content: Gaseous fuels are widely used in domestic, industrial, commercial, and automobile sectors because they provide efficient combustion, produce less smoke and ash, and can be easily controlled during burning. The commonly used gaseous fuels are Natural Gas, Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG).

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Gaseous fuels offer high thermal efficiency, cleaner combustion, low maintenance cost, and reduced environmental pollution compared to solid fuels.

items.question: Clean Combustion
items.answer: Burn with very little smoke, ash, and soot.

items.question: High Calorific Value
items.answer: Produce more heat per unit mass compared to many solid fuels.

items.question: Easy Control
items.answer: The rate of combustion can be controlled accurately.

items.question: Efficient Mixing
items.answer: Mix readily with air, resulting in complete combustion.

items.question: Environment Friendly
items.answer: Produce lower emissions of harmful pollutants.

content.content: Natural gas is a naturally occurring gaseous fossil fuel found beneath the earth's surface, usually associated with petroleum deposits. It is one of the cleanest fossil fuels and is extensively used for domestic, industrial, and power generation purposes.

items.question: Power Generation
items.answer: Used in gas turbine and combined cycle power plants.

items.question: Domestic Fuel
items.answer: Used for cooking and water heating through piped gas supply.

items.question: Chemical Industry
items.answer: Used in the manufacture of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen.

items.question: Industrial Heating
items.answer: Used in furnaces, boilers, and process heating.

content.content: LPG is a mixture of propane and butane that is liquefied under moderate pressure for convenient storage and transportation. It is colorless, odorless in pure form, and an odorant is added to detect leakage.

items.question: High Calorific Value
items.answer: Produces a large amount of heat on combustion.

items.question: Smokeless Flame
items.answer: Burns with a clean blue flame.

items.question: Easy Storage
items.answer: Stored in cylinders under pressure.

items.question: Portable
items.answer: Can be transported easily for domestic and commercial use.

content.content: LPG is widely used as a domestic cooking fuel, in hotels and restaurants, laboratories, industrial furnaces, metal cutting operations, and as an automobile fuel in some vehicles.

CNG is natural gas compressed to a very high pressure (about 200–250 bar) to reduce its volume for easy storage and transportation. It mainly consists of methane and is considered one of the cleanest automotive fuels.

items.question: Automobile Fuel
items.answer: Widely used in buses, cars, taxis, and auto-rickshaws.

items.question: Low Pollution
items.answer: Produces lower CO, NOx, and particulate emissions.

items.question: Economical
items.answer: Cheaper than petrol and diesel in many regions.

items.question: Engine Life
items.answer: Leaves very little carbon deposit, increasing engine life.

content.content: Comparison of Natural Gas, LPG and CNG

right_points: LPG stored as liquid in cylinders

items.question: High Efficiency
items.answer: Provide complete combustion with better thermal efficiency.

items.question: Clean Fuel
items.answer: Produce very little ash and smoke.

items.question: Easy Handling
items.answer: Can be transported through pipelines or cylinders.

items.question: Environmental Protection
items.answer: Emit fewer pollutants than coal and petroleum fuels.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Questions frequently ask the composition, advantages, and applications of Natural Gas, LPG, and CNG along with comparisons between them.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Gaseous fuels burn cleanly and efficiently.
LPG mainly consists of propane and butane.
CNG is compressed natural gas used mainly as automobile fuel.
Natural gas is supplied through pipelines.
LPG is stored as liquid under pressure in cylinders.
CNG produces lower emissions than petrol and diesel.
Gaseous fuels have high calorific value and low pollution.
